rows.note: Use this as the everyday all-purpose verb when fixing a time or place.

example.english: We agreed to appoint the meeting for three o'clock on Friday afternoon.
example.traditional: 我哋定咗星期五下晝三點開會。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ding6 zo2 sing1 kei4 ng5 haa6 zau3 saam1 dim2 hoi1 wui6

rows.note: Use this when the time or place is settled by agreement between people.

example.english: My friend and I agreed to appoint the meeting for tomorrow at the MTR station.
example.traditional: 我同朋友約定咗聽日喺地鐵站見。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 joek3 ding6 zo2 ting1 jat6 hai2 dei6 tit3 zaam6 gin3

rows.note: Use this when someone is officially named to a post or role.

example.english: The board will appoint him as the new principal.
example.traditional: 董事會任命佢做新校長。
example.jyutping: dung2 si6 wui6 jam6 ming6 keoi5 zou6 san1 haau6 zoeng2

rows.note: Use this for a formal appointment that entrusts someone with a position or authority.

example.english: The government makes a formal decision to appoint him as committee chair.
example.traditional: 政府正式委任佢做委員會主席。
example.jyutping: zing3 fu2 zing3 sik1 wai2 jam6 keoi5 zou6 wai2 jyun4 wui2 zyu2 zik6
